summary.headline: Divi's Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 64% YoY to ₹1,127 crore on total income of ₹3,770 crore, with management guiding only to double-digit revenue growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income for Q2 FY27 rose about 32% YoY to ₹3,770 crore, with PBT up 65% to ₹1,505 crore and PAT up about 64% to ₹1,127 crore. For H1, total income was ₹6,907 crore (vs ₹5,389 crore) and PAT ₹2,029 crore (vs ₹1,234 crore). Net material consumption fell to about 32% of sales from 40%, attributed to Custom Synthesis mix, Unit 3 backward integration and cost benefits. Operating cash flow weakened, which management tied to a large capex cycle, with CWIP at ₹1,638 crore.

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Contributed 38% of standalone sales in H1; management described performance as stable with healthy volume growth, though pricing pressure persists in some categories.

segments.name: Custom Synthesis (CS)
segments.commentary: Contributed 62% of standalone sales in H1; standalone revenue grew 17% YoY in constant currency for H1. Management said several programs are in validation or commercialization, with validation quantities supplied in Q2.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: H1 revenue ₹571 crore, up from ₹492 crore (about 16%). Management cited growing global demand for preventive healthcare and wellness ingredients.

segments.name: Peptides
segments.commentary: Management said several fragments are under validation or customer qualification; several 3,000 litre SPPS lines are being installed. Peptides are innovation-only, with no generic peptides at present.

guidance_outlook: Management guides to double-digit revenue growth; it declined to give a specific figure or comment on margins beyond that.
Asked about the 40%+ EBITDA margin in H1, management said it hopes margins are sustainable but gave no change to the prior 32-35% range.
Capex outlook of about ₹2,000 crore per year, plus or minus 20%, for the next two to three years, based on current RFPs.
Three dedicated CS projects: one is close to commercialization, and two are expected to commercialize over the next one to two quarters, subject to customer approvals.
capex_capacity: Q2 capitalization ₹772 crore; H1 capitalization ₹1,223 crore; CWIP ₹1,638 crore at 30 Sep 2026.
Historic capex run-rate about ₹2,000 crore per year (±20%) over the last three to four years post-COVID; management says forward RFPs support a similar level.
Installing several 3,000 litre SPPS lines for peptide programs; management says total SPPS capacity will place Divi's in the top three players with futuristic capacity, without disclosing current KL.
Unit 3 Kakinada supports backward integration into pre-chemistry and enables phased transfer of manufacturing from existing units; capex is said to be split roughly evenly across the three units.
Unit 1 has about 22 production blocks, Unit 2 about 25, and Unit 3 six; only three production blocks are dedicated across all units.
demand_pricing: Generic pricing pressure persists in certain categories, but volumes are growing; management noted a slight increase in usage growth.
Management says there is no capacity shortage now and none foreseen; plants are multipurpose, and CS capacity is planned with customers under long-term contracts.
Divi's handles about 60-70 CS projects at any time across pre-chemistry, qualification and later stages.
Asset turn for the overall basket is about 1.5x; management declined to split asset turns by peptides vs small molecules.

Input costs rose on petrochemical solvents; ocean freight and air freight costs rose due to Red Sea/Suez and Middle East disruptions. Company holds rolling three-month inventory for critical materials.

qa_highlights.question: What is the base business growth and margin excluding validation batch revenue in the CDMO business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify validation batch revenue, saying it is an ongoing business where validation leads to customer pick-up, qualification and commercialization; no split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Has the agency inspection for commercial batches been scheduled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no notice of inspection has been received; the agency may approve based on past history or require a pre-approval inspection, which will become clear once customers submit batches.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving volume growth of about 40% in CS, given muted raw material cost growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed lower material cost ratio (32% vs 40%) to a higher CS mix, Unit 3 backward integration and cost benefits; it did not name specific new products, citing confidentiality.

qa_highlights.question: How many validation batch projects are in validation or qualification?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was difficult to give a cumulative figure; around 60-70 projects are handled at any time across stages, and the three major investment projects are the only ones announced.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex be sufficient and what is the outlook for capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex outlook is about ₹2,000 crore ±20% per year, based on current RFPs; management says it builds capacity ahead only when opportunities are on the table.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow fall sharply relative to PBT growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the large capex cycle, including about ₹772 crore capitalized in Q2, and advances disbursed against the ₹1,638 crore CWIP.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company increase its EBITDA margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance remains double-digit revenue growth and it would not comment further on margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a bonus share proposal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said any such decision rests with the Board and would be communicated at the appropriate time.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow lagging PBT growth; H1 cash flow from operations before tax was ₹959 crore, down about 50% per an analyst. Working capital and inventory (₹5,325 crore) are rising.
Sacubitril/valsartan genericization (LOE around November 2026) could affect CDMO volumes; management declined to comment on specific customers.
Dependence on validation batches and the timing of regulatory approvals and commercialization for the three dedicated projects; management gave no firm dates.
Whether H2 growth holds at double digits after 17% constant-currency growth in H1, and whether margins stay above the prior 32-35% range.
Middle East and Red Sea disruptions raising solvent, freight and inventory costs; the company holds three months of critical raw material stock.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline numbers and capacity, but evasive on specifics: management repeatedly declined to quantify validation batch revenue, product-level volumes, SPPS capacity and margins, citing NDAs and confidentiality. Guidance was kept to double-digit revenue growth only.
key_quotes: All I can say is the CS business, and how Nilima has expressed CS business and the generic business, has about 62% is CS.
I would say it would be double-digit growth. That is my way forward that I would look at.
Historically, if you see the last three years post-COVID, three to four years, our capex outlook has been about ₹2,000 crores, plus or minus 20% every year.
We do not make generic peptides right now.

adds.what: Several 3,000 litre SPPS lines for peptide programs (capacity size not disclosed)
Unit 3 Kakinada backward integration into pre-chemistry, enabling phased transfer of manufacturing from existing units

growth.why: Management guides only to double-digit FY27 revenue growth with no margin figure, backed partly by three dedicated CS projects (one near commercialization, two expected within 1-2 quarters subject to customer approvals), several 3,000 litre SPPS lines being installed and about ₹2,000 crore annual capex (±20%) for 2-3 years, though SPPS capacity size is undisclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 net material cost fell to ~32% of sales from 40% on CS mix and Unit 3 integration, and management hopes 40%+ EBITDA margin is sustainable, but it kept the prior 32-35% range and gave no margin guidance.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Q2 capitalisation ₹772 crore, H1 ₹1,223 crore and CWIP ₹1,638 crore; several 3,000 litre SPPS lines are under installation, though capacity size is undisclosed and commissioning dates are not given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides to double-digit FY27 revenue growth, H1 CS standalone grew 17% in constant currency, and volumes in generics are growing, though pricing pressure persists in some categories.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex run-rate of about ₹2,000 crore per year (±20%) over 2-3 years is already guided on current RFPs, and CWIP of ₹1,638 crore signals an active build cycle; no new board-level plan beyond that was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was held at double-digit revenue growth only, with management declining to comment on margins, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Sacubitril/valsartan genericisation around November 2026 could hit CDMO volumes, rising solvent and freight costs from Red Sea and Middle East disruption, and operating cash flow lagging PBT growth, with H1 CFO before tax of ₹959 crore down about 50%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Three dedicated CS projects: one close to commercialisation and two expected to commercialise over the next 1-2 quarters subject to customer approvals, though no products were named.

rows.label: Peptide SPPS capacity and fragment qualification
rows.why: Several fragments are under validation or customer qualification and several 3,000 litre SPPS lines are being installed, but no commercial timing or capacity size was given.

rows.label: Nutraceuticals demand growth
rows.why: Global nutraceutical revenue rose to ₹571 crore in H1 from ₹492 crore (about 16%), with management citing rising preventive-healthcare demand.

rows.label: Backward integration at Unit 3 Kakinada
rows.why: Unit 3 backward integration into pre-chemistry is commissioned and is one of the drivers of the material cost ratio falling to ~32% from 40%.

tone.note: Management was confident on headline growth, capex and capacity, but declined to quantify validation batch revenue, product volumes, SPPS capacity and margins, citing confidentiality; analysts pressed on margin sustainability, base business growth and weak operating cash flow.
